rulesNotes: 45 general education + 42 business core + 18 Finance + 15 electives = 120 semester credits.

At least 12 upper-level area-of-study credits, the upper-level business capstone, and one additional three-credit upper-level course in the area of study or Professional Business Requirements. The six published Finance requirements are all upper level; the standard baseline also keeps upper-level FIN-3010 and BUS-4210 in the business core.

The 15-credit elective allowance includes selected MAT-1290 Precalculus and four unrestricted three-credit choices. MAT-1190 is an alternative prerequisite; the baseline does not require both math courses.
FIN-3210 and FIN-3820 formally require FIN-3010, STA-2010 and MAT-1190 or MAT-1290. This baseline retains the MAT-1290 option, including its MAT-1210 prerequisite.
The FIN-3820 advisory paragraph mentions MAT-1210, but its formal prerequisite block requires MAT-1190 or MAT-1290; advisory language is not substituted for the published formal requirement.
The current catalog exposes no academic-year edition label. Tuition and original transfer evidence have separate source-bound dates.
The 105-credit outside ceiling and 90-credit alternative-source ceiling are distinct. Only actual researched course allocations determine the proposed transfer total.
At least half the Finance area of study must be current within ten years of the most recent application date; the capstone has a five-year currency limit.
This Finance degree is not a professional license or a guarantee of professional examination eligibility.
Personal admission/catalog eligibility, course currency and future registration availability depend on the individual record.
Existing receiving-school awards retain their original provider, course-version, credit-unit, delivery and individual-evaluation conditions. No provider award is inferred from a course title.
This baseline uses standard nonmilitary residency; military, foreign-credit and Edison Accelerate scenarios need their applicable policies.
Published standard tuition is a provisional planning basis; provider subscriptions, books and applicable fees remain separate.
